citations.quote: We have not worked out whether that has anything to do with the draughty bathroom or is simply the season, so I mention it only for completeness.
We really need an independent building expert to look at it and say what the cause is, otherwise this argument will go on forever.
We propose that our caretaker, Mr Huber, visits the flat to assess the problem with the window.
He could come on Monday, 16 November 2026, between 9 and 11 a.m. Please confirm that access to the flat will be possible at that time.

plan.because: Needed to establish the parties, property and tenancy terms.
The customer reports notification in June, but the original report is missing.
The letter acknowledges a message but does not establish when the landlord received the defect report.
Dated objective evidence of the window and affected location is missing.
The supplied letter records a proposed visit and access request, but not the full response history or proposed repair work.
Mould is unmentioned and presumed absent for the evidence plan.
A heating fault is unmentioned and presumed absent for the evidence plan.
The possible connection between the husband's illness and the defect is expressly unresolved.
An independent expert is requested and the technical cause is disputed; request any existing inspection findings.
A rent deposit is unmentioned and presumed not considered for the evidence plan.
This is optional evidence under the process.

questions: Are there any urgent health or safety concerns requiring immediate attention?
What symptoms has your husband experienced, and has a health professional considered whether they may relate to the bathroom conditions?
When did the landlord receive your June report, and do you have the report and delivery evidence?
Did the proposed caretaker visit take place, and what responses, repair proposals or access arrangements followed?
Is an independent inspection report already available?
